issue: Is 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1), the federal ban on firearm possession by felons, constitutional under the Second Amendment as applied to people convicted of nonviolent felonies, and did Bruen abrogate pre-Bruen circuit precedent upholding the statute?

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) is constitutional in all its applications, including to nonviolent felons, because status-based disarmament of felons is consistent with the historical tradition. Pre-Bruen precedent upholding the statute need not be revisited.
cases: United States v. Hunt, 123 F.4th 697 (4th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Jackson, 110 F.4th 1120 (8th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Dubois, 94 F.4th 1284 (11th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Duarte, 137 F.4th 743 (9th Cir. 2025) (en banc)

sides.position: Bruen abrogated pre-Bruen circuit precedent upholding § 922(g)(1), so the statute must be tested under Bruen's text-history-and-tradition framework, and as-applied challenges can succeed.
cases: United States v. Range, 124 F.4th 218 (3d Cir. 2024) (en banc)
United States v. Diaz, 116 F.4th 458 (5th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Williams, 113 F.4th 637 (6th Cir. 2024)

this_court: Upholds § 922(g)(1) in all applications, including as applied to nonviolent felons, and takes the side that Bruen does not require displacing circuit precedent.
quote: In doing so, the majority deepens a circuit split, intentionally taking the broadest possible path to uphold § 922(g)(1).
cite: United States v. Steven Duarte, 137 F.4th 743 (9th Cir. 2025)
